title: Operator sprint: fallback design & triage notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working sprint-level artifact: compact triage guidance + fallback design notes for the most common API surface degradations we see in production (client request timeouts, 429s, degraded streaming, and elevated 5xx/error rates).

Audience: oncall SREs, service owners, solutions engineers. Not a final runbook — meant as a lightweight, operator-friendly checklist and design sketch we can iterate on during the next rotation.

High-level intent:
- Give responders 2-minute checks to stabilize traffic and stop customer-facing impact.
- Provide a short escalation path and temporary mitigation primitives (throttles, capacity re-route, degraded-mode features).
- Capture design ideas for automated fallback behavior to be considered by runtime and platform teams.

Quick triage checklist (first 2 minutes):
1) Confirm alert: which signal fired? (Pager duty, slack #sre-incident).
2) Scope: which route(s)/tenant(s)/region? Use: grafana -> Explore / search logs -> group_by route.
3) Check ingress pressure and backend health:
   - Metrics: redwood_api_request_rate{route}, redwood_api_error_rate{code}, redwood_api_latency_p50/p95/p99.
   - Dashboards: "API surface - latency & errors" and "Streaming QoS by route".
4) Immediate stabilization options (pick one, communicate in Slack):
   - Add temporary client-side rate-limiting rule (gateway) for noisy tenants.
   - Route small % of traffic to standby region/model variant (use routing policy: immediate-fallback).
   - Disable non-essential features (streaming, function-calls) via feature flags for the affected route.
5) If more than 5% of requests failing or latency > SLA for 10m -> escalate to on-call eng-sre lead and page platform-engineering.

Timeouts (symptoms): increased p95/p99 latency, client aborts, many partial responses in streaming logs.
Quick checks:
- Query: sum(rate(redwood_api_timeout_count[2m])) by (route,region,tenant)
- Check downstream model instance CPU/GPU and socket queue length.
- Look for long tail in KV cache hit-rate (prefix cache misses) causing recompute.
Mitigations (temporary):
- Short-term: reduce max-seq length or enforcible token caps via routing policy for impacted routes.
- If GPU saturation on Dedicated: trigger burst to other capacity pools (manual scaling via infra runbook ID INFRA-ops-run-3).
- If specific model is slow, failover to a smaller compatible model (policy: failover-model-compatible).
Notes for automation: consider a pressure-aware admission controller that trims sequence length based on current per-GPU concurrency.

429s (symptoms): sudden spike in 429 responses from gateway or runtime, correlated with request rate or bursty clients.
Quick checks:
- Count broken down by source IP/client-id or API key: sum(rate(redwood_api_429_count[1m])) by (api_key,route).
- Inspect token bucket fill level at gateway (if exposed).
Mitigations (temporary):
- Apply adaptive per-API-key soft-quota with short cooldown (60s).
- Implement short-lived client-side backoff suggestion via returned Retry-After header.
- If global throttling triggered because of downstream overload, open a narrow token-bucket window for high-priority keys only.
Design sketch: a graceful 429 handling flow that returns a JSON body with suggested backoff, optional queued-submission token, and a lightweight embedding-only fallback for latency-sensitive apps.

Degraded streaming (symptoms): slow chunk cadence, truncated streams, high client disconnects.
Quick checks:
- Streaming chunk delivery intervals vs expected: histogram of chunk_latency_seconds.
- Runtime logs showing partial writes or keepalive failures.
Mitigations (temporary):
- Flip streaming -> non-streaming synchronous response path (send final completed response instead of chunked).
- Reduce stream chunk size (configurable via route override).
- Increase proxy keepalive/timeouts between gateway and runtime for affected region.
Operator tip: use the 'force-sync' route override: POST /admin/route-override {route,mode:sync}. Requires infra auth.

Elevated error rates / 5xx spikes (symptoms): high 5xx percentage, often correlated with specific model variant, or with a recent deploy.
Quick checks:
- Is there a recent rollout? check rollout-tracking: deployment_id in the last 30m.
- Trace sampling: pull 10 traces for failing requests to see top exception messages.
Mitigations (temporary):
- Rollback recent rollout or promote previous stable model.
- Throttle traffic with a canary ratio (route -> canary 0% for failing flow).
- If errors are due to third-party service (e.g., KMS/timeouts to PG), circuit-break those calls at runtime and return degraded response.
Post-incident follow-ups (must-haves):
- Run a focused postmortem if: >1% of global requests affected, or any enterprise customer SLA breach.
- Capture the root cause hypothesis and actions taken in the incident ticket.
- Create a follow-up engineering task for any temporary mitigation left in place (ensure revert deadline).

Operator play snippets (copy-paste):
- Check top failing routes:
  curl -s "https://metrics-api.internal/query?expr=sum(rate(redwood_api_error_count{code=~\"5..\"}[5m])) by (route)" | jq

- Force sync mode override (internal API):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/v1/chat","mode":"sync"}' https://admin.internal/route-override

- Re-route 10% traffic to standby variant (k8s rollout patch):
  kubectl -n redwood patch svc routing-config --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/traffic","value":[{"variant":"stable","weight":90},{"variant":"standby","weight":10}]}]'

Communication templates (Slack):
- Incident bootstrap (short):
  [incident] severity=P2 route=/v1/chat region=us-west-2 signal=p95-latency owner=eng-sre
- Update example: "Investigating: p95 latency spike attributed to GPU queue growth on shard g3. Taking 10% traffic off shard and enabling sync-mode for impacted routes. ETA 10m."

Open questions / experiment log (for follow-up):
- Should runtime expose a per-request admission score we can use for smart short-circuiting?
- Can we design an async-queue fallback for batchable requests to avoid 429 storms?
- Experiment: implement temporary client token-leasing API that returns a small queued token so frontends can poll instead of hammering.

Follow-up action items (sprint backlog candidates):
- SRE: prototype admission trimming by sequence length and measure latency/cost tradeoffs. (owner: Ethan)
- Platform: policy engine endpoint that supports tenant-level prioritized bypasses for enterprise keys. (owner: Sofia)
- Runtime: add optional transparent sync-mode for streaming endpoints. (owner: Jonah)

Notes to self / operator heuristics:
- Use metrics and logs in parallel — sometimes dashboards hide bursty single-API-key storms.
- Avoid wide blast-radius changes early; prefer targeted throttles and routing tweaks.
- If unsure: default to routing a small % to standby or smaller model variant rather than global throttle.

References and artifacts:
- Incident ticket templates: confluence:templates/incident-runbook
- Backoff & retry design doc: confluence:design/retry-and-backoff-v3

Status: draft. Will iterate after next oncall rotation with real incidents and incorporate platform feedback.
